{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-jlb0","title":"accept_authenticated_schc_packet does not bind peer context to receiving link","description":"File: rust/lichen-schc/src/link.rs

accept_authenticated_schc_packet admits SCHC data if link.accepts_authenticated_frame(data_frame) and data_frame.sender pubkey equals peer.signer_identity(). Decompress then only checks retained DIO evidence is_current() (retirement flags).

It does not call peer.is_current_for(link). That check is what compress_schc_for_peer uses, and it is the full live binding: same receiving LinkLayer instance, peer still in the table, matching key-generation Arc, still pinned.

Without it, a caller can decode on link B using a DIO-issued AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext from link A, or keep using a context after the peer is unpinned/removed as long as the retirement atomics are still live. Python stores peer contexts on the LinkLayer and cannot do this. FragmentSender::new / policy.accepts_current already fail closed on the same binding.

Fix: require peer.is_current_for(link) (and signer match against the live evidence) before decompress, matching compress_schc_for_peer.","acceptance_criteria":"accept_authenticated_schc_packet returns InvalidPeerEvidence when the peer context was issued for a different LinkLayer instance, when the peer is no longer pinned or present, or when the DIO evidence is otherwise not accepted by the receiving link. compress_schc_for_peer and unfragmented accept use the same is_current_for gate.
